operational_root_cause.summary: The producer violated the workflow's own write scope on every dispatch, which failed every dispatch, which re-armed the dispatch.
the_loop: The charter's operational_revision_reason (factory-wide placement requirement) instructs the producer to write results/audit/frontier/<team>/CYCLE_<run_id>_GATE.json and reports/audit/frontier/<team>/CYCLE_<run_id>.md.
The team's own FROZEN RULES.json write_scope lists SEVEN paths, including those two audit directories.

But .github/workflows/frontier-team.yml 'Enforce team scope' (line 161) allows only SIX patterns -- frontier/$TEAM/*, tests/frontier/$TEAM/*, results/frontier/$TEAM/*, reports/frontier/$TEAM/*, state/frontier/$TEAM.json, data/frontier/$TEAM/*, plus the empty-string arm. The audit tree is absent. Charter acceptance test (12) likewise names only the five team trees plus the state file.
So the producer wrote the audit placement copies, the scope step built BAD and exited 4, and the producer job FAILED on every run from 38845649012 through 38851515402 (eight dispatches).
The following step, 'Persist team snapshot', is `if: always()`, so it committed the offending files anyway and produced a CLEAN tree -- indistinguishable from a successful no-op.

The lane then re-dispatched a charter that could only fail the same way. The loop was caused by neither missing evidence nor an open defect, and it was invisible to the team because every snapshot looked clean.
evidence: workflow line 161: case "$p" in "frontier/$TEAM"/*|"tests/frontier/$TEAM"/*|"results/frontier/$TEAM"/*|"reports/frontier/$TEAM"/*|"state/frontier/$TEAM.json"|"data/frontier/$TEAM"/*|"") ;; *) BAD+="$p\n";; esac
workflow line 162: [[ -z "$BAD" ]] || { echo -e "::error::Frontier crossed scope:\n$BAD"; exit 4; }
workflow line 164: the immediately following step is `if: always()` and runs `git add -A`

RULES.json write_scope = 7 entries (includes results/audit/... and reports/audit/...); the workflow allow-list = 6 patterns; charter test (12) = 5 trees + state file. Three different scopes, the workflow's the one that is enforced.
empirically: the tree carried 9 producer-authored CYCLE_*_GATE.json placement copies and 10 CYCLE_*.md copies, all git-tracked (i.e. committed by the if:always() persist step)

This cycle does not make it and does not need it: the independent audit of record (CYCLE_38841035773_GATE.json, gate=PASS) already exists in the audit tree, and the producer's disclosure now lives in scope. Recorded, not escalated.

harness_defect_repaired_38852056955.defect: The unfinished delta left by snapshot 38851515402 was red at 126 passed / 1 failed. test_scope_guard.py::_workflow_scope_patterns cut the workflow's case-arm list at the first ' ;;', which captures the shell case terminator glued to the final arm: the workflow writes its last arm literally as |"") so the token parsed as '"\")' instead of '""', and the empty-string arm assertion failed. The bug was in the TEST's parser, not in scope_guard.py: the guard's six prefixes are correct.
harness_defect_repaired_38852056955.fix: The parser now cuts the arm list at the shell case terminator: re.search(r'case "\$p" in\s*(.*?)\)\s*;;', step, re.S). re.S keeps it correct if the workflow is ever re-wrapped onto several lines. An explicit cardinality assertion (6 allow-list patterns + the empty-string arm == 7) was added so a truncated or over-broad parse fails with a clear message instead of only as a set mismatch.
why_this_is_not_benchmark_weakening: The anti-drift test was vacuous while red: it never reached its comparison. It now runs and PASSES on the true workflow file, which is a strictly stronger state.

Mutation-proved in a /tmp copy of the tree, three ways, all detected: widening the WORKFLOW allow-list (adding results/audit/frontier/$TEAM/*) FAILS; narrowing it (removing data/frontier/$TEAM/*) FAILS; widening the GUARD to match a widened workflow FAILS. The test is bidirectional, so neither side can drift alone.
The cardinality assertion fails closed (7 expected) rather than accepting whatever the parser produced.
RULES.json, the rubric, the thresholds and every previously accepted verdict are untouched; the parser reads a workflow file, not frozen rules.
